provenance.captured_via: initialize + tools/list through agent/integrations mcp_upstream, owner-approved (read-only server)
provenance.scrubbing: none needed: tool schemas carry no account or personal data

tools.name: wheelta_board_query
tools.description:
Query today's cash-secured-put board across 85 columns and return only what you ask for.

This is the entry point for any question about what to sell puts on. Filter on any
column (score, cushion, yield, greeks, IV, open interest, spread, technicals, support
and resistance, 52-week position, fund structure), sort on any column, page with
offset, and choose exactly which columns come back.

The board holds one row per symbol per DTE tenor, so a name can appear up to three
times — dedupe on `rowId`, group on `symbol`. The upstream API does no filtering of
its own, so a query is evaluated over the whole board: results are complete with
respect to your filters, not a first page of a server-side search.

Set `groupBy` when the question is about the board's shape ("which sectors dominate",
"how do scores differ by tenor") — it returns counts and means instead of rows, for a
fraction of the tokens. Call wheelta_board_fields for the column catalog and worked
examples; use wheelta_board_row for one candidate's full drawer.

filters.description: Conditions, ANDed. Omit to match every row.
filters.title: Filters

select.description: Columns to return. Omit for a sensible screening set. Ask for only what you need — this is the main lever on how much context a result costs.
select.title: Select

sort_by.description: Column to order by. Any numeric, date or text column.
sort_by.title: Sort By

offset.description: Rows to skip — page through a large match
offset.title: Offset

group_by.description: Summarise instead of listing: return one entry per distinct value of this column with row counts and metric means. Far cheaper than rows when the question is about shape rather than specific candidates.
group_by.title: Group By

metrics.description: Numeric columns to average per group
metrics.title: Metrics

field.description: Column path, e.g. 'sector', 'risk.cushionCoverage', 'technicals.adx'. Call wheelta_board_fields for the catalog.
field.title: Field

op.description: 'between' takes [low, high] inclusive; 'in'/'notIn' take a list; 'contains' is a case-insensitive substring on text; 'isNull'/'notNull' take no value.
op.title: Op

tools.name: wheelta_board_fields
tools.description:
List the columns wheelta_board_query can filter, sort and select on.

Call this before composing a non-obvious query, or when a column name was rejected.
Each entry gives the column's type, unit, whether it can be null and what a null
means there, the allowed values for enum columns, and whether it is sortable.

Needs no network call — the catalog is derived from the contract this server is
pinned to. `examples` shows complete worked queries.

search.description: Filter the catalog by substring against column path, description or unit — e.g. 'cushion', 'volatility', 'fund'. Omit for all 85.
search.title: Search

tools.name: wheelta_board_row
tools.description:
Open one board candidate's detail drawer, section by section.

Use after wheelta_board_query has narrowed to a name, or when asked about a specific
ticker. Sections are opt-in so a question about technicals does not also pay for a
page of news prose.

`wheelIq.explanation.groups[]` decomposes the score exactly — baseline plus the seven
themes' impactPoints sums to the score with no residual. Explain a score from that,
and read `impactPoints` rather than `score` when saying what drove it: a theme can
score 90 and barely move the total if it carries little weight.

404s when the symbol is not on today's board, or has no row in the requested bucket.
That is a real answer about the board, not an outage.

symbol.description: Ticker, uppercase, 1-5 letters. Dotted or class-share tickers (BRK.B) are not addressable in this API.
symbol.title: Symbol

bucket.description: Which tenor row. Omit for the symbol's primary row — its highest-scoring tenor.
bucket.title: Bucket

sections.description: Which parts of the drawer to return. Defaults to the scored sections (wheelIq, quote, contract, risk). 'technicals' adds the indicator set, 'levels' support/resistance, 'range' the 52-week position, 'trend' ~30 trailing closes, 'catalysts' the dated events, 'news' the AI news read (~9 KB of prose, written once a day — ask for it only when the question is about news, sentiment or event risk). 'all' returns everything.
sections.title: Sections

tools.name: wheelta_board_status
tools.description:
Report how fresh today's board is and how the screening funnel narrowed to it.

The cheapest call in this server — a few hundred tokens, no rows. Use it to answer
"how current is this?", to check whether a rebuild has landed, or before a long
analysis. `buildId` identifies the funnel build and is not advanced by the 5-minute
quote merge, so it — not `asOf` — is what changes on a real rebuild. `nextRefreshAt`
is the poll target.

Builds run at 07:45, 10:00, 12:00, 14:00 and 15:30 America/New_York.

tools.name: wheelta_assignment_rates
tools.description:
Report what actually happened to contracts the board previously recommended, sliced
by one dimension.

One row per settled contract, with its entry snapshot taken at first board sighting.
Defaults to cushionBand because cushion is what dominates the outcome.

This is descriptive history, not a model: publish `assignedRateLow`/`High` alongside
any rate, and publish `meta.pending` — most persisted contracts have not expired yet,
so a large pending count means the sample is early rather than that assignment is
rare. Buckets with `reliable: false` are provisional. An empty sample returns zeroed
counts, not an error.

category.description: Which dimension to slice settled contracts by
category.title: Category

lookback_days.description: Sample window. Snapped UP to 30, 90, 180 or 365 upstream; the value actually used comes back in meta.lookbackDays.
lookback_days.title: Lookback Days

tools.name: wheelta_macro_snapshot
tools.description:
Return the current macro picture and its wheel-strategy regime verdict.

Answers "is this a good environment for selling puts right now?" and gives the
backdrop for any board result. `regime` carries the tag, a plain-language summary,
explicit guidance, and the exact FRED inputs the classification was computed from, in
rule-test order.

Most indicators come from a 24-hour cache; six are refreshed per request from live
sources and are listed in `liveIndicatorIds`. Values are in native units with `change`
in the same unit and `changePct` as a decimal fraction.

category.description: Restrict indicators to one category: rates, inflation, volatility, recession, labor or markets. Omit for all of them.
category.title: Category

tools.name: wheelta_macro_series
tools.description:
Return one FRED macro series as a time series, thinned to fit a model context.

Use for trend questions the snapshot cannot answer — where rates or the yield curve
have been heading, not just where they are. Points are ascending by date. Thinning
keeps the first and last points and spaces the rest evenly; ask for a longer window
rather than more points when you need shape rather than precision.

series_id.description: FRED series id, e.g. DGS10, T10Y2Y, VIXCLS, UNRATE
series_id.title: Series Id

lookback_days.description: Days of history. Rounded UP to the nearest 30/90/180/365/730/1095/1825 bucket upstream, so you may receive slightly more than requested.
lookback_days.title: Lookback Days

max_points.description: Thin the series to at most this many points
max_points.title: Max Points

tools.name: wheelta_candles
tools.description:
Return daily OHLCV bars for one underlying.

Use for price-action questions a board row cannot answer — how a name has traded into
the current setup, where it sat before a move. When the requested window holds more
bars than `maxPoints`, bars are aggregated into equal buckets (open of the first, max
high, min low, close of the last, summed volume) rather than sampled, so highs and
lows survive; `aggregated` says when that happened.

Today's bar is still forming and lags intraday. For a current price use
wheelta_quotes, or `quote.price` on a board row.

symbol.description: Ticker, uppercase, 1-5 letters. Dotted or class-share tickers (BRK.B) are not addressable in this API.
symbol.title: Symbol

max_points.description: Aggregate down to at most this many bars
max_points.title: Max Points

tools.name: wheelta_quotes
tools.description:
Return the latest quote tick for a set of symbols.

Read from an in-memory tick buffer that refreshes on a 60-second cadence during market
hours, so this is the freshest price this API exposes. Use it for current prices,
including for symbols not on the board; use wheelta_candles for history.

Symbols with no tick come back in `missing` rather than as an error or a null price.

items.description: Ticker, uppercase, 1-5 letters. Dotted or class-share tickers (BRK.B) are not addressable in this API.

tools.name: wheelta_correlations
tools.description:
Return pairwise correlation of daily log returns across a set of symbols.

Use to check whether a shortlist is actually diversified before treating it as one.
Two names both scoring well on the board can be nearly the same bet; this is how you
find that out.

Upstream bounds global concurrency on this route tightly, so ask once for the whole
set rather than issuing many small calls. Fails with history_unavailable when fewer
than two symbols' histories resolve.

items.description: Ticker, uppercase, 1-5 letters. Dotted or class-share tickers (BRK.B) are not addressable in this API.

tools.name: wheelta_calendar_events
tools.description:
Return upcoming earnings and ex-dividend dates for symbols the board covers.

This is the event-risk check to run before committing to a candidate: an earnings
print inside the contract's life is the single most common reason a screened setup is
a bad idea. Ex-dividend dates matter for assignment timing on dividend payers.

Scoped to the board's universe, so a symbol the screener does not cover will not
appear. Events come back ascending by date.

items.description: Ticker, uppercase, 1-5 letters. Dotted or class-share tickers (BRK.B) are not addressable in this API.

symbols.description: Restrict to these tickers. Omit for all.
symbols.title: Symbols

in_window_only.description: Only events inside a symbol's trade window
in_window_only.title: In Window Only

tools.name: wheelta_company_research
tools.description:
Return one company's identity and its valuation snapshot in a single call.

Profile gives name, sector, industry, description, exchange and country. Valuation
gives the multiples (P/E, PEG, P/B, P/S, EV/EBITDA), EPS, dividend yield and payout,
beta, and the 52-week range with the current position inside it.

Use to answer "what is this company and is it expensive?" about a board candidate.
You do not need this to label a board row: rows already carry `company`, the same
string this returns as `companyName`.

The two halves come from different providers and are fetched concurrently; if one is
unavailable the other is still returned, and `unavailable` says which failed.

symbol.description: Ticker, uppercase, 1-5 letters. Dotted or class-share tickers (BRK.B) are not addressable in this API.
symbol.title: Symbol
